title: Foster's own chronology 1922 to 1929: St. Louis, boat, Chicago, Louis Russell
summary: Foster lists leaving the boat for the coast in 1922, St. Louis, Creath, Dewey Jackson, Chicago and Louis Russell until 1940.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I quit the boat and come out here in 22. Over in the center for me out here in 22. Yeah.
That's when you played tuba for a while then out here. No, no.
I played tuba here for a while. Did I have a tuba when I first came out here? Yeah. I had my tuba. I had a brass tuba. The same tuba that I sold it to Albert Morgan.
Then you went back to the boat after you'd been here in 22. Is that right? No.

Let me see what did I do. 22. I went back and joined Charlotte Crispin. I left here and went to St. Louis. I joined Charlotte Crispin. Then in 23, I joined the quit Charlotte Crispin band and went with Dewey Jackson band on the boat back to New Orleans. 24, I came on back to St. Louis. Left St. Louis, went on back to New Orleans, joined City Days Band. Still was sitting in the Daz Bean Band until 27. Mudd Carey said for me to come back out here to join him, where he was in Chicago. See?
Yeah, that's that picture where you were playing tuba.

Then I played for the Elves Parade. I was at a convention in Chicago. And I went on to Chicago. Passed through St. Louis, told Dewey I'd be back. That's when Johnny wanted me to stay with him. With all them kids. See? I joined the Drew Jackson band and stayed with the Drew Jackson band then from September 28th until February 29th. I went to the Louis Russell band. I stayed with Louis Russell. That fills that. I stayed with Louis Russell until 1940. That's when Joe fired the whole band for the Chief of Band. He got them kids out of Philadelphia.
